Lecture topics: Great Migration, history of unionization in the United States, de-industrialization, outsourcing of labor, globalization, rise of fascism in Italy, history of New York City, history of immigration to the United States, machismo, Black American culture in the 1990s, gun violence in the United States.

The article discusses why the labor market for working class New Yorkers has dwindled and moved other places. 00:03:14 Ken discusses that these issues are country wide but the readings for his course focus on New York. 00:04:06 Ken discusses the positive elements of New York, including its willingness to struggle and the belief to make something possible. He mentions Ralph Ellison's Invisible Man and the immigration from the South to the North in the United States. 00:11:30 Ken discusses this migration further and connects it to the economic situation in New York with disappearing jobs. He discusses the beginnings of this change as starting in the 1920s when New York was a city with many small manufacturing enterprises. These factories employed people. But the jobs left because "cultural leaders," or people with money, who had a vision for New York that never came to fruition and didn’t include these working people. Ken describes this vision as New York being a financial center for the country, real value in buying and selling land, which knocked factories out. Ken attributes this being a part of the reason why rent has gone up. 00:14:44 Ken continues to discuss land value as it relates to service industries. He defines Wall Street as a service industry. "Which industries will be funded in order to prosper?" Ken describes this way of industry operating as like gambling. 00:16:05 Ken introduces the legalization of unions in the 1930s by President Roosevelt into the conversation. Ken discusses how capitalists saw workers unionization efforts and desire for better wages and benefits as mechanisms that cut into their profits. Ken attributes this to why jobs left New York and moved South before unionization was there. Then around the world. 00:17:54 Ken mentions a similar pattern to contemporary [1990s] times with computer programming jobs. 00:18:30 Ken continues discussing how American workers are competing with workers overseas, in worse conditions, and how this led to Americans living on debt. 00:19:57 Ken discusses the article In Search of New York from the 1987 special issue Dreams of the Future from the "leftist" magazine Dissent. 00:21:35 Ken discusses the cultural modernism style of movies from the 1920s and 1930s and its transformative effect on society. Ken discusses how these artists called themselves futurists and believed that "nothing is more beautiful than a machine; nothing is more beautiful than a speeding car; nothing is more beautiful than war." Ken believes Futurists utilized rapid exposures to create movement in their art. 00:24:47 Ken transitions the conversation to New York, the invention of elevators, and skyscrapers. 00:26:04 Ken continues to speak of New York and the plan for it as a vertical city with cool sidewalks and the integration of it into one conglomerate city. Ken connects this back to the loss of jobs and opportunities in the city. 00:28:25 Ken discusses benign neglect to get working class families to leave to acquire that land and build more industry. Ken connects urban renewal to this concept as well. 00:30:07 Ken discusses Battery Park City which he describes as a wealthy enclave with their own mayors. Ken discusses how everyday people in New York subsidize the standard of living for those in Battery Park City. 00:31:10 Ken discusses the economy and how money is being stolen from working class peoples. He mentions the book The Betrayal of Democracy by William Greider who discusses the breakdown of American politics, special interests, and parties. Title#1: Jacobs, Ken - The Impossible (Collective for Living Cinema)
Abstract#1: Talk by Ken Jacobs at the Collective for Living Cinema about The Impossible, a series of Nervous System performances. Topics discussed include: TOM TOM THE PIPER'S SON, Hanz Hoffman, 3D visuals and imagery. Also includes questions and feedback from the audience

Note#2: 00:00 Audio starts with a snippet of a news broadcast. It is between an interviewer and a 12-year-old boy who says he is high on marijuana. Another voice interrupts the interview to provide context regarding the interview and introduce the legal and medical debate around the use of marijuana. 00:35 Audio of discussion begins in the middle of a conversation. 02:30 Ken begins discussing Tom Tom the Piper's Son. Ken discusses having trouble following the story. Describes the film as pre-conscious and non-directed. 04:21 Ken takes an audience question regarding story. Ken believes the story is in some ways about the character Tom coming into his sexuality. Describes the film as “unfocused erotic content” and containing “polymorphous perversity.” 07:00 Ken discusses how the film entertains "whole new dimensions of observation." 08:04 Ken takes another audience question regarding movement in the film. Ken discusses wanting to see this style of film in more mainstream and contemporary film. 13:50 More audience questions.
